## Description
**What**: Ship plugins/dso/config/known-antipatterns.yaml as an append-only registry with a documented versioned schema (id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, citation), document it in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and implement plugins/dso/hooks/check-known-antipatterns.sh as a thin wrapper over static-defense-lib.sh that reads the registry via a single pinned parser (python3 or yq, parser choice independent of yq v3-vs-v4 syntax), blocks staged content matching any registry entry (seeded with the declare -A bash-4-only class), enforces the append-only contract (reject removal or mutation of an existing entry), ships its per-hook baseline, and registers in .pre-commit-config.yaml between shellcheck and pre-commit-review-gate.
**Why**: The registry is the data-driven extension point consumed by downstream epics (99f1-153c, d63f-2c74, a47f-b451); it must publish a stable versioned schema and tolerate the empty-registry case before those consumers run.
**Scope**:
- IN: the registry file and its versioned schema, the CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md documentation, the hook, the append-only mechanical guard, the pinned-parser choice, the initial baseline, the .pre-commit-config.yaml entry, and the fixture + end-to-end test.
- OUT: populating the registry beyond the seed entry (owned by 99f1-153c); downstream consumer wiring.

## Done Definitions

- check-known-antipatterns.sh blocks a commit when staged content matches a registry entry (seed: declare -A in a bash-3.2-target script) read from known-antipatterns.yaml ← Satisfies: sc-1
- known-antipatterns.yaml ships as an append-only registry with a documented versioned schema carrying id, pattern, target languages/dirs, remediation, and citation fields, documented in CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md, and a commit that removes or mutates an existing registry entry is rejected ← Satisfies: sc-4
- check-known-antipatterns.sh reads its per-hook count-based baseline so captured existing violations do not block while a new instance beyond the baseline is blocked ← Satisfies: sc-2
- check-known-antipatterns.sh emits a per-file diagnostic naming the offending line, the remediation string, and the registry-entry citation ← Satisfies: sc-3
- check-known-antipatterns.sh honors a non-empty `# bash4-only:` or `# antipattern-ok: <reason>` suppression and rejects an empty or whitespace-only suppression reason ← Satisfies: sc-5
- a fixture test asserts detection on staged content, baselined-violation non-firing, new-instance blocking, and baseline-growth rejection; an end-to-end test invokes the hook through the real pre-commit framework and the hook resolves its own path, baseline, and registry without CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT and passes its own check (dogfood) ← Satisfies: sc-6
- check-known-antipatterns.sh and its registry parsing execute under a bash-3.2-constrained test that passes ← Satisfies: sc-8
- unit tests (fixture-based) are written and passing for all new detection, registry-parsing, and append-only-guard logic in check-known-antipatterns.sh ← Satisfies: sc-4

## Considerations

- [Hermeticity] The hook MUST resolve its own path, baseline, and registry location via BASH_SOURCE -> readlink -f, never CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT.
- [Parser] Use a single pinned parser (python3 or yq); the parser choice must not depend on yq v3-vs-v4 syntax differences — no new dependency (yq and python3 already available).
- [Consumer] Publish the registry with a stable, documented, versioned schema before downstream consumers (99f1-153c, d63f-2c74, a47f-b451) run; consumers must tolerate the empty (not-yet-populated) registry case.
- [Build] check-known-antipatterns.sh and its new test files must have the executable bit set.
- [Merge-safety] Register as a discrete, independently-named entry in the shellcheck-to-pre-commit-review-gate band; CONFIGURATION-REFERENCE.md edits target a disjoint section.

## Escalation Policy

**Escalation policy**: Proceed unless a significant assumption is required to continue — one that could send the implementation in the wrong direction. Escalate only when genuinely blocked without a reasonable inference. Document all assumptions made without escalating.
data.title: As a developer, I want an append-only known-antipatterns.yaml registry plus check-known-antipatterns.sh that reads it to block staged registry-defined antipatterns, so new antipattern classes are detected and the registry is mechanically guarded
